slot.brief: Given a spring–mass SHM with stated amplitude and spring constant, find the kinetic energy at a specified displacement, or the ratio KE:PE there.

stem: A $0.20$ m amplitude spring–mass oscillator has spring constant $200$ N m$^{-1}$. What is its kinetic energy when its displacement from the mean position is $0.12$ m?
solution:
For a spring–mass oscillator, $K=\frac12 k(A^2-x^2)$. Substituting the given values,
$$K=\frac12(200)(0.20^2-0.12^2)=2.56\ \text{J}$$
